tour.title: Project Overview
tour.description: Start with README.md to understand DiziDental as a clinic Hospital Management System built with Spring Boot and React. The document outlines the monorepo layout (backend, frontend, Docker), core modules like patients, appointments, and billing, and how to get the dev environment running. Pair it with .env.example to see the environment variables that wire the frontend to the backend API and database at runtime.

tour.title: Backend Entry Point
tour.description: ClinicHmsApplication.java is the Spring Boot bootstrap that starts the entire HMS backend via SpringApplication.run. On startup, DataSeeder loads demo organizations, doctors, and patients so you can explore the system immediately, while application.properties configures the PostgreSQL datasource, JPA settings, JWT secret, and file-upload limits that every downstream service relies on.
tour.languageLesson: Spring Boot's @SpringBootApplication combines @Configuration, @EnableAutoConfiguration, and @ComponentScan so a single main class discovers and wires the entire application context.

tour.title: Security & Authentication
tour.description: Before any clinical data is accessed, the security layer gates every request. SecurityConfig defines a stateless JWT filter chain with CORS rules and public login routes. AuthController handles mobile-and-password login, issuing an HTTP-only JWT cookie and bootstrapping module permissions, while JwtAuthenticationFilter validates that token on every subsequent request and populates the Spring Security context.
tour.languageLesson: Spring Security's filter chain runs before controllers: each filter can authenticate, authorize, or reject a request, and stateless JWT setups avoid server-side session storage entirely.

tour.title: Patient Domain & Visits
tour.description: Patients are the central entity in the clinic model — the Patient JPA entity maps demographic and org-scoping fields to PostgreSQL tables defined in init-db.sql. VisitController exposes REST endpoints for listing, creating, and auto-generating patient visits, delegating business rules to VisitService which ties each visit to a patient, doctor, and organization context.
tour.languageLesson: JPA entities like Patient use @Entity and @Table annotations to map Java fields to relational columns; Spring Data repositories then provide type-safe database access without raw SQL.

tour.title: Appointment Scheduling
tour.description: Building on the visit model, appointments add time-slot scheduling to the clinic workflow. AppointmentController provides CRUD endpoints for listing by date, creating, rescheduling, and cancelling appointments, while AppointmentService enforces owner-scoped queries, slot validation, and real-time event publishing. On the frontend, ScheduleView.jsx renders the calendar UI that consumes these endpoints to manage the clinic day.

tour.title: Billing & Payments
tour.description: After clinical work is recorded on a visit, billing converts treatment procedures into invoices. BillingController exposes endpoints to list billable items from visit treatments, create bills, fetch the latest bill, and record payments. BillingService derives line items from treatment data, persists bills via JPA, and publishes billing events. BillingView.jsx on the frontend drives the full invoice-creation, payment-recording, and print-preview workflow.

tour.title: Frontend Entry Point
tour.description: The React client bootstraps from main.jsx, which mounts the root App component inside StrictMode with global styles applied. App.jsx is the top-level shell: it checks backend connectivity, holds authentication state from the JWT cookie, and conditionally renders either the login page or the role-aware dashboard based on the user's session.
tour.languageLesson: React 18's createRoot API replaces the legacy ReactDOM.render; StrictMode double-invokes effects in development to surface side-effect bugs early.

tour.title: Dashboard & API Client
tour.description: Once authenticated, UnifiedDashboard.jsx acts as the role-aware shell that routes users to the correct module views based on their permissions, wrapping every major clinic page in a shared WowDash layout. LoginPage.jsx handles the credential form that calls the backend auth endpoint. The shared api.js Axios client — the most-imported frontend module — attaches the API base URL and JWT cookie to every request, connecting all pages to the Spring Boot backend from Step 2.

tour.title: Key Patient Pages
tour.description: The patient module is the most-used area of the UI for day-to-day clinic work. HeaderPatientSelector lets staff pick the active patient from anywhere in the app, and PatientOverviewPage shows the selected patient's summary, visits, and quick actions. PatientSchedulePage surfaces that patient's upcoming appointments, completing the loop between the backend visit/appointment APIs from Steps 4–5 and the frontend dashboard shell from Step 8.

tour.title: Container Deployment
tour.description: The dev environment ships as Docker containers orchestrated by docker-compose.yml, which wires the PostgreSQL database, Spring Boot backend, and React frontend into a single stack. Each service has its own multi-stage Dockerfile: the backend image compiles with Temurin JDK 21 and runs the bootJar on JRE 21 exposing port 8080, while the frontend image builds with Node.js and serves the Vite production bundle through nginx on port 80.
tour.languageLesson: Multi-stage Docker builds use separate FROM stages: the builder stage includes compilers and dev dependencies, while the final stage copies only runtime artifacts, typically reducing image size by 50–80%.
